requirement: Generate a sitemap.xml for a website with lxml, producing a namespaced, correctly escaped UTF-8 document that respects the sitemap protocol limits.
skeleton: A sitemap namespace, a URL limit, a default nsmap, a frozen Page dataclass, and build_sitemap creating urlset and url elements with SubElement, validating loc and priority, and serialising with an XML declaration.
caption: Building a sitemaps.org XML file with lxml etree.Element and SubElement instead of string formatting. Page is a frozen dataclass of loc, optional lastmod date and optional priority. build_sitemap(pages) raises ValueError past MAX_URLS of 50000, creates urlset in the sitemap namespace with a default-namespace nsmap so no ns0 prefix appears, and for each page raises ValueError unless loc starts with http:// or https://. It adds url with loc, lastmod as an ISO date when set, and priority formatted to one decimal when set, raising ValueError outside 0.0 to 1.0, letting lxml escape text. It returns etree.tostring with xml_declaration=True and UTF-8 encoding. The fixture asserts the declaration and default namespace, child order, escaping of ampersands and angle brackets, raw UTF-8 output, rejection of relative locs, inclusive priority bounds, the exact URL limit, and an empty sitemap.

plan.intent: Publish a sitemap for search engine crawlers
constraints: The urlset uses the sitemap namespace as the default namespace
Priority must be within 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive, else ValueError
Output is UTF-8 with an XML declaration and escaped text

rationale.teaches: Build XML with Element and SubElement in a namespace with a default nsmap and let tostring handle escaping, encoding and the declaration.
rationale.why: String-built XML breaks on ampersands, a missing nsmap yields ns0 prefixes crawlers reject, and missing declarations or ASCII entity output confuse strict parsers.

ops.docstring: Build a sitemaps.org XML document with lxml SubElement.

candidates.why_wrong: Without a default nsmap every element is written with an ns0 prefix.
A sitemap with exactly 50000 URLs is rejected although the protocol allows it.
Priorities of exactly 0.0 or 1.0 are rejected as out of range.
The output lacks the XML declaration and encodes non-ASCII characters as entities.
Relative locations are written into the sitemap and crawlers cannot resolve them.
